blocks.text: This page tracks the Abbotsford MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $702,800 for a typical home, down 9.9% over twelve months.
Abbotsford benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Abbotsford home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $702,800 in October 2026. That is little changed at +0.1% on the month, down 3.0% over three months, down 5.7% over six months and down 9.9% over the year. Over three years it is down 11.5%, and over five years down 13.3%.
The weakest one-year move in Abbotsford was for a detached home homes at −13.1%; the strongest was an apartment at −10.0%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,090,500) and an apartment ($370,300) is $720,200, and a townhouse ($579,600) sits $209,300 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $860,000, Abbotsford is 18.3% below. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 6.4% against down 9.9% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, Abbotsford ranks 7 by all-home benchmark, with Mission above it at $787,800 and North Surrey below it at $637,000.

Detached homes in Abbotsford: benchmark $1,090,500, little changed at +0.3% in a month, down 4.6% in three months, down 8.1% in six months, down 13.1% in a year, down 9.1% in three years and down 12.4% in five. That is 15.7% below the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,293,800).

Townhouse homes in Abbotsford: benchmark $579,600, down 2.2% in a month, down 3.7% in three months, down 5.1% in six months, down 10.1% in a year, down 10.3% in three years and down 3.2% in five. That is 21.9% below the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($742,300).

Apartment homes in Abbotsford: benchmark $370,300, little changed at +0.0% in a month, down 2.8% in three months, down 7.5% in six months, down 10.0% in a year, down 13.7% in three years and little changed at −0.8% in five. That is 19.6% below the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($460,800).

blocks.text: Set against October 2025, Abbotsford had 72 detached sales (54 a year earlier), 42 townhouse sales (50 a year earlier) and 47 apartment sales (50 a year earlier). Month-end active listings were 400 detached (about 480 a year earlier), 214 townhouse (about 225 a year earlier) and 321 apartment (about 367 a year earlier). Dividing sales by active listings gives a sales-to-active ratio of 18.0% for detached, 19.6% for townhouse and 14.6% for apartment.

In dollars, the typical Abbotsford home is worth about $77,200 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $780,000. By type, detached homes lost about $164,400, from $1,254,900 to $1,090,500, townhouses lost about $65,100, from $644,700 to $579,600, and apartments lost about $41,100, from $411,400 to $370,300 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $745,300 six months ago and near $794,100 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $42,500 below the six-month mark and about $91,300 below the three-year mark. Against the Fraser Valley Board area, the Abbotsford benchmark is about $157,200 below the regional $860,000; a year earlier the difference was about $138,800 below.
Abbotsford sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 591 Abbotsford houses sold at a median of $1.05M (middle half $921,406 to $1.25M), half of them within 23 days. 510 condos sold at a median of $385,000 (middle half $315,000 to $445,000), half within 35 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $1.09M to $1.02M between November–January and August–October (119 and 146 sales).

blocks.text: What the Abbotsford figure is
The $702,800 Abbotsford figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Fraser Valley Real Estate Board for October 2026.
